item.research_question: What are the unique elastic and plastic deformation mechanisms of a single-phase BCC NbTaTiV refractory high-entropy alloy at room temperature and elevated temperatures, and how do they compare to conventional BCC alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc melting under argon atmosphere from 99.99% purity elements, melted 10 times, drop-cast into 4-mm diameter rods, sealed in quartz tubes, homogenized at 1200°C for 3 days, followed by water cooling.
item.test_conditions: In situ neutron diffraction compression tests at RT, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C with strain rate of 1 × 10−4 s−1; Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (RUS) from 100 to 650 kHz; First-principles DFT calculations at absolute zero and RT; Machine Learning predictions; HAADF-STEM imaging of 15% deformed samples.
key_findings: Yield strength decreased from 1064 MPa at RT to 595 MPa at 900°C.
Work-hardening exponent decreased from 0.2732 at RT to 0.1199 at 900°C.
The alloy exhibits elastically isotropic deformation behavior at RT (Zener anisotropy AZ ≈ 1.2, Universal anisotropy index AU = 0).
Elastic anisotropy gradually increases at elevated temperatures but shows much smaller variation (AZ from 1.2 at RT to 1.6 at 900°C) compared to conventional alloys.
The dominant mobile dislocations during plastic deformation are edge dislocations (<111> {110}), unlike conventional BCC metals where screw dislocations often dominate.
Single-crystal elastic constants calculated via DFT show good agreement with experimental neutron and RUS data, with relative errors of -15.9% (Young's), -16.6% (shear), and -6.0% (bulk) at RT.
The alloy maintains a single BCC solid solution phase with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm up to 900°C.
Pugh ratio (K/G) and Poisson's ratio (ν > 0.26) indicate the material is intrinsically ductile.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that the severely distorted lattice in the HEA, caused by the random distribution of multiple elements with different atomic radii, leads to compositional fluctuations that deviate edge dislocation cores from their neutral planes. This creates wavy dislocation lines, which substantially reduces the mobility of edge dislocations, making them the dominant mobile character compared to conventional BCC metals where edge dislocations annihilate easily.
item.limitations: The text notes that the validity of theoretical calculation methods for designing elastically isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs was previously lacking experimental validation, though this paper addresses that. It also mentions that the ML model predictions are somewhat unexpected because the Materials Project database contains ordered compounds, not disordered alloys like HEAs, and lattice distortion effects might cause less accurate results.
item.future_work: The authors state these discoveries may facilitate the development of possible alloy systems for structural material applications and provide a road map toward the discovery and production of newly designed polycrystalline materials.
quotes: The dominant type of mobile dislocations during plastic deformation could be edge dislocations, which is different from conventional BCC metals.
The NbTaTiV HEA exhibits the unique elastic isotropic deformation behavior at RT.

The severely distorted lattice induces the deviation of the formation of dislocations from their neutral dislocation planes, which, consequently, leads to a substantial reduction in the mobility of edge dislocations during plastic deformation.
